key_insight: BiVerify improves mathematical self-correction by requiring the same candidate solution to pass both backward constraint checks and forward reasoning verification.
engineering_relevance: Bidirectional verification offers a reusable workflow for checking both constraint satisfaction and reasoning completeness in AI-assisted mathematical problem solving.
method: Start with backward verification against the original constraints, then check the reasoning forward.
Dynamically switch directions, reset verification state, and revise until the same candidate passes both checks.
Use shared mathematical tools to separate logical reasoning from precise computation.
evidence_signal: Across five challenging math benchmarks and multiple DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini models, BiVerify reports a 13.5-percentage-point average accuracy gain over the strongest representative public baseline evaluated, reaching 31.2 points on GPT.
watch_item: Iterative verification may add latency and computation cost; passing both checks is not a formal guarantee of correctness.
paper_title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
